environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind AWS ALB with an attached AWS WAF WebACL. The WebACL includes a custom rate-based rule (threshold: 5 requests per 5-minute window per source IP, scoped to URI path '/api/v2/directory/*') that returns HTTP 429 before traffic reaches the target group. Additionally, an AWS WAF custom rule with priority 1 uses a regex pattern set matching LDAP metacharacters in request body and query string fields (pattern: '[)(|*\\][)(|*\\]' — consecutive LDAP special characters) with BLOCK action. The rate-based rule evaluation window uses a sliding window with IP address aggregation from X-Forwarded-For after CloudFront (trusted proxy depth: 1). Note: the regex rule targets double-metacharacter sequences only, as single parentheses appear in normal JSON payloads.

config.infrastructure: AWS ALB + WAF WebACL -> ECS Fargate (Flask on port 8080)
config.rate_limit_behavior: Once 5 requests from same IP hit /api/v2/directory/* within 300s window, all subsequent requests from that IP to those paths receive 429 for remainder of window. First 5 requests pass through.
config.ldap_server: OpenLDAP 2.4, same config as exploitable env
config.network: ALB SG: CloudFront-managed-prefix-list:443; ECS SG: ALB-SG:8080; LDAP SG: ECS-SG:389
